source.title: Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization
source.anchor: First equality in chain continuing Theorem 2.13 proof. Same gradient-square sum carried on both sides.

slots.1_objects_spaces: Scalar sequences a,w:Nat to Real. Distance specialization x:Nat to E, comparator u:E, real steps eta and natural horizon in a normed additive commutative group E. Euclidean space is an instance. Only real numbers obtained from squared norms participate in the rearrangement; no inner product on E, completeness or finite dimension required.
slots.2_quantifiers_order: Generic forall a,w,T, if 0<T then equality. Distance forall E and instance, x,u,eta,T, if 0<T and forall t<T, 0<eta(t), then equality. Fixed comparator for all rounds, trajectory arbitrary, no hidden optimizer.
slots.3_assumptions: Positive horizon, plus positivity of played rates in distance statement. No sign/order imposed on generic weights. Distance algebra uses total real division and does not invoke hη. The full theorem assumes feasibility, convex differentiable losses, bounded diameter and positive nonincreasing steps; those are not required for this isolated equality.
slots.4_conclusion: Exact identity: with q_t=norm(x(t)-u)^2, w_t=1/(2 eta(t)), sum_{t<T}(q_t-q_{t+1})w_t=q_0w_0-q_Tw_{T-1}+sum_{t<T-1}(w_{t+1}-w_t)q_{t+1}. Generic theorem has arbitrary q=a and w.
slots.5_constants_indices: Lean x(0)=source x_1, x(T)=source x_(T+1), eta(T-1)=source eta_T. Initial plus, terminal minus, next-minus-current reciprocal increment applied to next squared distance. Factor 1/2 multiplies entire interior sum. Source gradient-square addend cancels from both sides.
slots.6_probability_feedback: Deterministic pathwise identities. Arbitrary x in production. OGD and also policy OSD are tested on actual algorithm-generated trajectories. This particular policy ignores history and selects fixed feedback(t).
slots.7_boundaries_exclusions: T=1 free terminal at same rate as initial, empty interior. T=0 outside exact statements. Positive eta only on played rounds, generic signed and zero weights permitted, unconstrained terminal. Equalities alone do not supply a regret inequality or diameter bound.

reconstruction.objects: a and w are arbitrary real sequences indexed by natural numbers, T is a natural horizon.
reconstruction.quantifiers_order: For every a, w, T, if T>0 then the identity holds.
reconstruction.constants_indices: Last weight is w_{T−1}; last sequence value is a_T. Interior coefficients multiply a_{t+1}.
reconstruction.exceptions: Signs, zeros and order of the weights are unrestricted. No terminal value is prescribed. T=1 is included, T=0 lies outside the hypothesis.

reconstruction.objects: E is a normed additive commutative group. x:ℕ→E is arbitrary, u∈E is fixed across t, η:ℕ→ℝ, and T∈ℕ.
reconstruction.quantifiers_order: For every such E, x, u, η and T, assume the two premises, then the equality holds.
reconstruction.constants_indices: The factor 1/2 applies to the entire interior sum; the last denominator is 2η_{T−1}.
reconstruction.stochastic_feedback_structure: No feedback, update rule, projection, or probability model is imposed on x.
reconstruction.exceptions: η is positive only on rounds t<T; no ordering of the rates is assumed. The terminal x_T is free. No Hilbert or finite-dimensional structure is required.

reconstruction.objects: The fixed sequences A=signedA and W=signedW with A_t=4 for t≥3 and W_t=1 for t≥2.
reconstruction.quantifiers_order: Closed statement with the indicated finite sums.
reconstruction.constants_indices: T=3; left summands are 0,−8,−5. Right side is 0−4+(−6−3).
reconstruction.exceptions: Includes a zero and a negative weight, and keeps the signed terminal contribution.

reconstruction.objects: Two arbitrary natural-indexed real sequences a and w.
reconstruction.quantifiers_order: For all a, w; horizon fixed at 1.
reconstruction.constants_indices: Only t=0 contributes on the left. Both endpoints use w_0.
reconstruction.exceptions: a_1 is free. The terminal term can be nonzero even when the interior sum is empty.

reconstruction.objects: a is a natural-indexed real sequence, c∈ℝ and T∈ℕ.
reconstruction.quantifiers_order: For all a,c,T with T>0, the four claims hold jointly.
reconstruction.constants_indices: Endpoint indices are 0 and T. The T−1 interior differences vanish.
reconstruction.exceptions: c is arbitrary including zero or a negative real; a_T is unrestricted.

reconstruction.objects: V is the full real line. g(t) is fixed to 1 at 0, −2 at 1 and 2 thereafter. η(t) is 2 at 1 and 1 otherwise. f_t(z)=g(t)z is real valued. x_t=ogd(t) is the iterate of projected gradient descent from x_0=0.
reconstruction.quantifiers_order: Closed theorem for these particular functions. The regularity and feedback properties quantify over natural t<3. The monotonicity test scopes the comparison to t+1<3.
conclusion: It is false that for all natural t with t+1<3, η(t+1)≤η(t). The increase at t=0 witnesses this.
For every t<3, f_t is convex on V and differentiable (ambient differentiability at the point) at every x in V.
For every t<3, the gradient of f_t at ogd(t) equals g(t).
reconstruction.constants_indices: Comparator u=2, horizon T=3. D=(4,9,1,1), L=(4−9)/2+(9−1)/4+(1−1)/2. C=(1/2)[(1/2−1)9+(1−1/2)1]. Terminal x_3 is an output after the final update using η(2).
reconstruction.stochastic_feedback_structure: Deterministic full-loss iteration. The update projects x_t−η(t)∇f_t(x_t) to V, which is the full line.
reconstruction.exceptions: This is an equality of distance-potential terms on the stated OGD trajectory. There is no quantified regret, loss-gap, expectation, or all-trajectories inequality. Regularity/feedback checks bind t=0,1,2; x_3 occurs only as a terminal iterate in the trajectory and distance identity.

reconstruction.objects: V is the full real line. g(t) is fixed to 1 at 0, −2 at 1 and 2 thereafter. η(t) is 2 at 1 and 1 otherwise. F_t(z) is the extended-real embedding of g(t)z+0. The policy returns g(t). x_t=osd(t) is the last point of its projected history starting at x_0=0.
reconstruction.quantifiers_order: Closed theorem for these particular functions. The regularity and feedback properties quantify over natural t<3. The monotonicity test scopes the comparison to t+1<3.
conclusion: It is false that for all natural t with t+1<3, η(t+1)≤η(t). The increase at t=0 witnesses this.
For every t<3, F_t never takes −∞, is equal to a finite real at some point, and at each x in V there exists s such that F_t(x)+⟨s,y−x⟩≤F_t(y) for every ambient y.
The feedback is legal through horizon 3: at every round t<3 the actually selected s_t at x_t satisfies F_t(x_t)+⟨s_t,y−x_t⟩≤F_t(y) for every real y.
For every t<3, the policy's actual selection s_t equals g(t).
reconstruction.constants_indices: Comparator u=2, horizon T=3. D=(4,9,1,1), L=(4−9)/2+(9−1)/4+(1−1)/2. C=(1/2)[(1/2−1)9+(1−1/2)1]. Terminal x_3 is an output after the final update using η(2).
reconstruction.stochastic_feedback_structure: Deterministic selection. A general policy receives t, the losses with indices <t, the history of t+1 outputs up to x_t, and the current full loss. This particular policy ignores all but t. The next output is the projection of x_t−η(t)s_t.
reconstruction.exceptions: This is an equality of distance-potential terms on the stated OSD trajectory. There is no quantified regret, loss-gap, expectation, or all-trajectories inequality. Regularity/feedback checks bind t=0,1,2; x_3 occurs only as a terminal iterate in the trajectory and distance identity.

originalProofRoutes.generic: Commute factors; Finset.sum_range_by_parts on w and consecutive differences; telescope prefixes with Finset.sum_range_sub'; distribute, telescope increments via Finset.sum_range_sub and collect endpoints by ring.
originalProofRoutes.distance: Instantiate generic declaration with norm distance squared and reciprocal doubled step, normalize division and move 1/2 outside sum. Source hη is retained without being used by the algebraic proof.

witnesses.oneRound: All a,w. Both endpoints use w(0), range 0 sum vanishes, a(1) remains free.
witnesses.constantZero: All a,c,T>0. Full identity for arbitrary c, reduced (a(0)-a(T))*c; full identity separately with zero, reduced zero.
witnesses.common: eta=(1,2,1) positive, nonincrease fails at 0. feedback=(1,-2,2). Full-line projection is identity; starting 0 gives -1,3,1. Comparator 2 gives q=(4,9,1,1). Left sum -5/2+2+0=-1/2. Initial 2, terminal -1/2, correction (-9+1)/4=-2, total -1/2.
witnesses.OGD: Real linear inner-product loss. linear_regular and regular_to_feasible establish feasible convexity and pointwise ambient differentiability; gradient_linear gives gradient at each played iterate. iterateVariable and step with project_fullSpace generate actual four outputs. distance_potential_sum_eq applied to that iterate.
witnesses.OSD: Extended-real affine loss with zero intercept; affine_proper and affine_subdifferential establish global properness and nonempty subgradients on the full line. Actual selection equals feedback by definition, hence LegalFeedback at actual rounds through horizon 3. output_zero and output_succ with project_fullSpace generate trace. distance_potential_sum_eq applied separately to policy output.
